questions.question: [Cybersecurity • Test 1 • Q1] In TLS/SSL handshakes, why is asymmetric encryption (RSA/ECC) used initially rather than for bulk data transmission?
options: Symmetric encryption keys cannot be stored in RAM.
Asymmetric algorithms can only encrypt up to 64 bytes total.
Symmetric encryption is vulnerable to packet loss.
Asymmetric cryptography is computationally expensive; it is used only to securely exchange a symmetric session key for fast bulk encryption.
questions.correctAnswer: Asymmetric cryptography is computationally expensive; it is used only to securely exchange a symmetric session key for fast bulk encryption.
questions.explanation: Asymmetric key exchange securely establishes identity and shared secrets, after which AES (symmetric) encrypts streams at gigabit line speeds.
questions.hint: Asymmetric for key agreement; symmetric for line-rate data.
questions.relatedConcept: Cybersecurity - Asymmetric vs Symmetric Encryption
questions.interviewTip: Modern TLS 1.3 mandates Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE) for Perfect Forward Secrecy.

questions.question: [Cybersecurity • Test 1 • Q2] What is the primary defense against SQL Injection vulnerabilities in web applications?
options: Client-side regex validation on input fields.
Parameterized queries / Prepared statements that separate SQL commands from user input data.
Base64 encoding all query parameters.
Replacing single quotes with double quotes.
questions.correctAnswer: Parameterized queries / Prepared statements that separate SQL commands from user input data.
questions.explanation: Prepared statements pre-compile SQL queries in the database engine, treating user input strictly as literal values rather than executable SQL.
questions.hint: Pre-compiled query parameters prevent code injection.
questions.relatedConcept: Cybersecurity - SQL Injection Mitigation
questions.interviewTip: Never concatenate user input into raw SQL queries.

questions.question: [Cybersecurity • Test 1 • Q3] How does an Anti-CSRF token protect authenticated state-changing POST requests?
options: Encrypts the entire HTTP body using AES-256.
Forces user passwords to expire every 15 minutes.
Stores session IDs in public query parameters.
Provides a unique, cryptographically random per-session secret that attacker domains cannot read due to Same-Origin Policy.
questions.correctAnswer: Provides a unique, cryptographically random per-session secret that attacker domains cannot read due to Same-Origin Policy.
questions.explanation: Browsers automatically send cookies with cross-site requests, but an unauthorized site cannot inject the unpredictable CSRF token required in the request payload.
questions.hint: Unpredictable secret token validated on server.
questions.relatedConcept: Cybersecurity - Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
questions.interviewTip: Combine Anti-CSRF tokens with SameSite=Lax/Strict cookie attributes.

title: Embedded Systems - Test 1: Core Fundamentals & Patterns
description: Comprehensive technical evaluation for Embedded Systems covering runtime mechanics, design principles, and problem solving.

questions.question: [Embedded Systems • Test 1 • Q1] In IoT telemetry, what delivery guarantee is provided by MQTT Quality of Service Level 1 (QoS 1)?
options: Guarantees exactly-once delivery with zero duplicates.
Fire-and-forget with no delivery confirmation (QoS 0).
Encrypts payload with end-to-end homomorphic encryption.
Guarantees message is delivered at least once to the broker, but duplicates may occur if ACK is delayed.
questions.correctAnswer: Guarantees message is delivered at least once to the broker, but duplicates may occur if ACK is delayed.
questions.explanation: QoS 0 is at most once, QoS 1 is at least once (requires PUBACK), and QoS 2 is exactly once (four-step handshake).
questions.hint: QoS 1 = At least once delivery.
questions.relatedConcept: Embedded Systems - MQTT Protocol QoS Levels
questions.interviewTip: Use QoS 0 for frequent temperature telemetry; use QoS 1/2 for critical actuator control.

questions.question: [Embedded Systems • Test 1 • Q2] Why must dynamic memory allocation ('malloc') and blocking delay loops be avoided inside an ISR?
options: Microcontrollers do not have physical RAM for ISRs.
ISRs execute in non-reentrant interrupt context where blocking stalls higher-priority events and malloc can cause non-deterministic latency or deadlock.
ISRs only run in low-power sleep modes.
Interrupt controllers only accept assembly code.
questions.correctAnswer: ISRs execute in non-reentrant interrupt context where blocking stalls higher-priority events and malloc can cause non-deterministic latency or deadlock.
questions.explanation: ISRs must be brief and deterministic. Long operations should be deferred to a background task or RTOS worker thread via flags or queues.
questions.hint: Keep ISRs fast, non-blocking, and deterministic.
questions.relatedConcept: Embedded Systems - Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) Constraints
questions.interviewTip: Always qualify shared ISR variables with the 'volatile' keyword.

questions.question: [Embedded Systems • Test 1 • Q3] Which hardware characteristic distinguishes the I2C bus from the SPI bus?
options: I2C is full-duplex while SPI is strictly simplex.
SPI requires 8 pull-up resistors per peripheral.
I2C can reach 100 MHz speeds while SPI is limited to 100 kHz.
I2C uses only 2 open-drain lines (SDA, SCL) with pull-up resistors and addressing; SPI uses 4 lines (MOSI, MISO, SCK, CS) with dedicated chip-selects.
questions.correctAnswer: I2C uses only 2 open-drain lines (SDA, SCL) with pull-up resistors and addressing; SPI uses 4 lines (MOSI, MISO, SCK, CS) with dedicated chip-selects.
questions.explanation: I2C conserves pin count via 7/10-bit software addressing on 2 wires, whereas SPI delivers higher throughput via dedicated Chip Select lines and full-duplex lines.
questions.hint: 2 wires (SDA/SCL) vs 4 wires (MOSI/MISO/SCK/CS).
questions.relatedConcept: Embedded Systems - I2C vs SPI Bus Protocols
questions.interviewTip: Use SPI for high-speed sensor data (displays, IMUs) and I2C for low-pin-count telemetry.

questions.question: [VLSI & Digital Electronics • Test 1 • Q1] What causes a Setup Time (T_setup) violation in synchronous sequential flip-flops?
options: Data input fails to remain stable for the required duration before the active clock edge arrives.
Clock frequency is too low for the CMOS gate.
Data input changes immediately after clock edge.
Supply voltage exceeds maximum breakdown.
questions.correctAnswer: Data input fails to remain stable for the required duration before the active clock edge arrives.
questions.explanation: Setup time is the minimum time data must be stable before the clock edge. If combinational path delay is too long, a setup violation occurs.
questions.hint: Data must be stable before the clock edge.
questions.relatedConcept: VLSI & Digital Electronics - Setup and Hold Time Violations
questions.interviewTip: Fix setup violations by reducing combinational logic depth or lowering clock frequency.

questions.question: [VLSI & Digital Electronics • Test 1 • Q2] What is the primary contributor to dynamic power dissipation (P_dynamic) in digital CMOS circuits?
options: Subthreshold leakage current through turned-off transistors.
Gate oxide tunneling breakdown.
Capacitive charging and discharging of load capacitance during output logic transitions (P = C * V^2 * f).
Thermal vibration of silicon crystal lattice.
questions.correctAnswer: Capacitive charging and discharging of load capacitance during output logic transitions (P = C * V^2 * f).
questions.explanation: Dynamic power is quadratic with supply voltage (Vdd^2) and linear with switching frequency (f) and load capacitance (C).
questions.hint: P = C * V^2 * f during gate switching.
questions.relatedConcept: VLSI & Digital Electronics - CMOS Inverter Static vs Dynamic Power
questions.interviewTip: Lowering Vdd provides the greatest reduction in dynamic power due to the squared term.

questions.question: [Finance • Test 1 • Q1] How is Net Working Capital calculated on a company's balance sheet?
options: Current Assets minus Current Liabilities.
Total Assets minus Total Liabilities.
Operating Revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold.
Gross Profit minus Capital Expenditures.
questions.correctAnswer: Current Assets minus Current Liabilities.
questions.explanation: Net Working Capital measures short-term liquidity and operational operational solvency over a 12-month horizon.
questions.hint: Current Assets - Current Liabilities.
questions.relatedConcept: Finance - Working Capital Ratio & Solvency
questions.interviewTip: A current ratio (Current Assets / Current Liabilities) between 1.5 and 2.0 indicates healthy liquidity.

questions.question: [Finance • Test 1 • Q2] In DCF valuation, what discount rate is used to discount Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF)?
options: Federal Reserve risk-free rate only.
Cost of Equity (CAPM) alone without debt weighting.
Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC), reflecting the blended cost of debt and equity financing.
Annual inflation rate (CPI).
questions.correctAnswer: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC), reflecting the blended cost of debt and equity financing.
questions.explanation: FCFF represents cash available to all capital providers (debt and equity), so it must be discounted using the blended corporate WACC.
questions.hint: Blended cost of debt and equity = WACC.
questions.relatedConcept: Finance - Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Valuation
questions.interviewTip: Use Cost of Equity when discounting Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE).

questions.question: [Finance • Test 1 • Q3] In options trading and financial derivatives, what does the option 'Delta' represent?
options: The rate of change of the option price relative to a $1 change in the underlying asset's price.
The rate of time decay per trading day (Theta).
The sensitivity of option price to changes in volatility (Vega).
The maximum potential financial loss.
questions.correctAnswer: The rate of change of the option price relative to a $1 change in the underlying asset's price.
questions.explanation: Delta ranges from 0 to 1 for call options and 0 to -1 for put options. It also approximates the probability of expiring in-the-money.
questions.hint: Price change per $1 move in underlying asset.
questions.relatedConcept: Finance - Option Greeks & Delta
questions.interviewTip: At-the-money options typically have a Delta close to 0.50.

questions.question: [Digital Marketing • Test 1 • Q1] In digital business models, what is considered an ideal Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) to Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) ratio?
options: 1:1 (break-even per acquisition).
0.5:1 (spending 2x customer lifetime value).
100:1 (no marketing expenditures).
3:1 (LTV is 3x greater than CAC), indicating healthy profitability and capital efficiency.
questions.correctAnswer: 3:1 (LTV is 3x greater than CAC), indicating healthy profitability and capital efficiency.
questions.explanation: A 3:1 ratio balances strong return on acquisition spend with adequate reinvestment in marketing growth channels.
questions.hint: Ideal benchmark is 3:1.
questions.relatedConcept: Digital Marketing - CAC to LTV Ratio Health
questions.interviewTip: LTV:CAC below 1.0 means the business loses money on every acquired customer.

questions.question: [Digital Marketing • Test 1 • Q2] In Human Resource Management, what defines the OKR (Objectives and Key Results) methodology?
options: Annual subjective manager feedback rating from 1 to 5.
Qualitative, ambitious Objectives paired with 3-5 quantitative, measurable Key Results tracked across cycles.
Strict salary deduction penalties for missed tasks.
Mandatory daily timesheet logging software.
questions.correctAnswer: Qualitative, ambitious Objectives paired with 3-5 quantitative, measurable Key Results tracked across cycles.
questions.explanation: OKRs connect team goals to organizational strategy with transparent, measurable outcomes (e.g. 'Increase checkout conversion from 2% to 3.5%').
questions.hint: Ambitious Objectives + Measurable Key Results.
questions.relatedConcept: Digital Marketing - OKR Framework in Performance Management
questions.interviewTip: OKRs should be decoupled from direct compensation to encourage ambitious target setting.

title: Stock Market - Test 1: Core Fundamentals & Patterns
description: Comprehensive technical evaluation for Stock Market covering runtime mechanics, design principles, and problem solving.

questions.question: [Stock Market • Test 1 • Q1] How is Net Working Capital calculated on a company's balance sheet?
options: Total Assets minus Total Liabilities.
Operating Revenue minus Cost of Goods Sold.
Gross Profit minus Capital Expenditures.
Current Assets minus Current Liabilities.
questions.correctAnswer: Current Assets minus Current Liabilities.
questions.explanation: Net Working Capital measures short-term liquidity and operational operational solvency over a 12-month horizon.
questions.hint: Current Assets - Current Liabilities.
questions.relatedConcept: Stock Market - Working Capital Ratio & Solvency
questions.interviewTip: A current ratio (Current Assets / Current Liabilities) between 1.5 and 2.0 indicates healthy liquidity.

questions.question: [Stock Market • Test 1 • Q2] In DCF valuation, what discount rate is used to discount Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF)?
options: Federal Reserve risk-free rate only.
Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC), reflecting the blended cost of debt and equity financing.
Cost of Equity (CAPM) alone without debt weighting.
Annual inflation rate (CPI).
questions.correctAnswer: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC), reflecting the blended cost of debt and equity financing.
questions.explanation: FCFF represents cash available to all capital providers (debt and equity), so it must be discounted using the blended corporate WACC.
questions.hint: Blended cost of debt and equity = WACC.
questions.relatedConcept: Stock Market - Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Valuation
questions.interviewTip: Use Cost of Equity when discounting Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE).

questions.question: [Stock Market • Test 1 • Q3] In options trading and financial derivatives, what does the option 'Delta' represent?
options: The rate of time decay per trading day (Theta).
The sensitivity of option price to changes in volatility (Vega).
The maximum potential financial loss.
The rate of change of the option price relative to a $1 change in the underlying asset's price.
questions.correctAnswer: The rate of change of the option price relative to a $1 change in the underlying asset's price.
questions.explanation: Delta ranges from 0 to 1 for call options and 0 to -1 for put options. It also approximates the probability of expiring in-the-money.
questions.hint: Price change per $1 move in underlying asset.
questions.relatedConcept: Stock Market - Option Greeks & Delta
questions.interviewTip: At-the-money options typically have a Delta close to 0.50.

questions.question: [Product & Project Management • Test 1 • Q1] If a startup has $1,200,000 in bank balance and net monthly burn rate of $75,000, what is its remaining runway?
options: 8 months
12 months
24 months
16 months (Runway = Total Cash / Net Monthly Burn).
questions.correctAnswer: 16 months (Runway = Total Cash / Net Monthly Burn).
questions.explanation: Runway calculation ($1,200,000 / $75,000 = 16 months) dictates how long operations can sustain before needing additional funding or reaching cash-flow positivity.
questions.hint: Cash / Net monthly burn rate.
questions.relatedConcept: Product & Project Management - Startup Runway & Burn Rate
questions.interviewTip: Start fundraising at least 6 months before runway expires.

questions.question: [Product & Project Management • Test 1 • Q2] In modern Product Management, how is the RICE score calculated to prioritize roadmap initiatives?
options: (Revenue * Innovation) / Cost
(Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
Risk + Impact + Cost + Execution
(Reach + Speed) * Profit
questions.correctAnswer: (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
questions.explanation: RICE standardizes feature evaluation by factoring user reach, business impact, estimation confidence, and developer effort.
questions.hint: (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort.
questions.relatedConcept: Product & Project Management - RICE Prioritization Framework
questions.interviewTip: Confidence score helps discount features backed by assumption rather than empirical data.

questions.question: [Product & Project Management • Test 1 • Q3] What causes the Bullwhip Effect in supply chain operations?
options: Physical conveyor belt breakdowns in shipping warehouses.
Seasonal weather events stopping shipping vessels.
Currency exchange rate fluctuations in global trade.
Small fluctuations in consumer retail demand cause progressively amplified order variability upstream to wholesalers and manufacturers.
questions.correctAnswer: Small fluctuations in consumer retail demand cause progressively amplified order variability upstream to wholesalers and manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Lack of visibility, order batching, and safety stock buffering at each supply chain layer create severe upstream demand distortion.
questions.hint: Small retail demand shifts cause amplified upstream swings.
questions.relatedConcept: Product & Project Management - The Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chains
questions.interviewTip: Information sharing and Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) dampen the bullwhip effect.

description: Comprehensive technical evaluation for Operations & Supply Chain covering runtime mechanics, design principles, and problem solving.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q1] Why do database storage engines (InnoDB, Postgres) utilize B+ Trees instead of standard Binary Search Trees?
options: B+ Trees eliminate all disk writes.
High fan-out minimizes disk I/O depth (O(log_B N)), and linked leaf nodes allow sequential range scans.
Binary trees cannot store string keys.
B+ Trees automatically compress data in RAM.
questions.correctAnswer: High fan-out minimizes disk I/O depth (O(log_B N)), and linked leaf nodes allow sequential range scans.
questions.explanation: B+ Trees store records only in linked leaves. The wide branching factor (high fan-out) reduces tree height to 3-4 levels for millions of rows.
questions.hint: High fan-out reduces disk page reads.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - B+ Tree Indexing & Range Lookups
questions.interviewTip: Understand covering index (index-only scan) optimization for SQL queries.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q2] What is the primary purpose of the Circuit Breaker pattern in microservice architecture?
options: Encrypts payload traffic with TLS.
Balances network load across all containers.
Compresses JSON responses.
Fails fast when downstream services become unresponsive, preventing cascading thread starvation across the system.
questions.correctAnswer: Fails fast when downstream services become unresponsive, preventing cascading thread starvation across the system.
questions.explanation: Circuit Breakers track failure rates and trip Open to reject requests immediately, returning fallback responses until health recovers.
questions.hint: Fails fast to protect system resilience.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - Microservices Circuit Breaker Pattern
questions.interviewTip: Always define fallbacks and reasonable timeout thresholds for HTTP clients.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q3] What causes Thrashing in Operating System memory management?
options: CPU clock speed throttled due to temperature.
Main memory is overloaded, causing the OS to spend more time swapping pages to disk than executing process instructions.
Network sockets buffer overflow.
Deadlock among mutual exclusion locks.
questions.correctAnswer: Main memory is overloaded, causing the OS to spend more time swapping pages to disk than executing process instructions.
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when active working sets exceed physical RAM, causing continuous page faults and disk I/O thrashing.
questions.hint: Continuous page faults and disk swapping.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - OS Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
questions.interviewTip: Working set model prevents thrashing by ensuring processes have sufficient page frames.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q4] What is the sequence of control flags exchanged during the standard TCP connection establishment?
options: ACK -> SYN -> FIN
SYN -> ACK -> DATA
RST -> SYN -> ACK
SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK
questions.correctAnswer: SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK
questions.explanation: Client sends SYN with initial sequence number (ISN), Server responds with SYN-ACK, Client sends ACK to establish full-duplex session.
questions.hint: Synchronize, Synchronize-Acknowledge, Acknowledge.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - TCP 3-Way Handshake & Flow Control
questions.interviewTip: TCP 3-way handshake sequence is a universal computer network interview question.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q5] In SOLID principles, what does the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) enforce?
options: Every class must inherit from exactly one parent.
Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without altering program correctness.
Classes should be open for modification and closed for extension.
Dependencies must be hardcoded statically.
questions.correctAnswer: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without altering program correctness.
questions.explanation: LSP guarantees that derived classes honor the contract and behavior expectations established by the base type.
questions.hint: Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - Object Oriented Design & SOLID Principles
questions.interviewTip: Violating LSP often occurs when overriding methods with empty implementations or unexpected exceptions.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q6] In Distributed Storage, how does Consistent Hashing minimize partition migration when a node is added?
options: Rehashes all keys across all servers from scratch.
Duplicates all partitions to every machine in cluster.
Freezes all transactions until rebalancing completes.
Maps servers and keys to a 360-degree hash ring, so adding a node only migrates k/N keys from its immediate neighbor.
questions.correctAnswer: Maps servers and keys to a 360-degree hash ring, so adding a node only migrates k/N keys from its immediate neighbor.
questions.explanation: Consistent Hashing ensures that only adjacent ring segments are redistributed, minimizing network transfer during cluster scaling.
questions.hint: Hash ring bounds key migration to immediate neighbors.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - Consistent Hashing in Distributed Systems

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q7] Which SQL transaction isolation level prevents Dirty Reads and Non-Repeatable Reads, but may allow Phantom Reads?
options: READ COMMITTED
REPEATABLE READ
READ UNCOMMITTED
SERIALIZABLE
questions.correctAnswer: REPEATABLE READ
questions.explanation: Repeatable Read locks scanned rows preventing updates, but standard SQL allows concurrent transactions to insert new matching rows (phantoms).
questions.hint: Read Uncommitted < Read Committed < Repeatable Read < Serializable.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - ACID Isolation & Concurrency Anomalies
questions.interviewTip: Serializable eliminates all anomalies via strict range locking or SSI.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q8] Why do database storage engines (InnoDB, Postgres) utilize B+ Trees instead of standard Binary Search Trees? (Variant 1.8)
options: B+ Trees eliminate all disk writes.
Binary trees cannot store string keys.
B+ Trees automatically compress data in RAM.
High fan-out minimizes disk I/O depth (O(log_B N)), and linked leaf nodes allow sequential range scans.
questions.correctAnswer: High fan-out minimizes disk I/O depth (O(log_B N)), and linked leaf nodes allow sequential range scans.
questions.explanation: B+ Trees store records only in linked leaves. The wide branching factor (high fan-out) reduces tree height to 3-4 levels for millions of rows.
questions.hint: High fan-out reduces disk page reads.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - B+ Tree Indexing & Range Lookups
questions.interviewTip: Understand covering index (index-only scan) optimization for SQL queries.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q9] What is the primary purpose of the Circuit Breaker pattern in microservice architecture? (Variant 1.9)
options: Encrypts payload traffic with TLS.
Fails fast when downstream services become unresponsive, preventing cascading thread starvation across the system.
Balances network load across all containers.
Compresses JSON responses.
questions.correctAnswer: Fails fast when downstream services become unresponsive, preventing cascading thread starvation across the system.
questions.explanation: Circuit Breakers track failure rates and trip Open to reject requests immediately, returning fallback responses until health recovers.
questions.hint: Fails fast to protect system resilience.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - Microservices Circuit Breaker Pattern
questions.interviewTip: Always define fallbacks and reasonable timeout thresholds for HTTP clients.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q10] What causes Thrashing in Operating System memory management? (Variant 1.10)
options: CPU clock speed throttled due to temperature.
Network sockets buffer overflow.
Deadlock among mutual exclusion locks.
Main memory is overloaded, causing the OS to spend more time swapping pages to disk than executing process instructions.
questions.correctAnswer: Main memory is overloaded, causing the OS to spend more time swapping pages to disk than executing process instructions.
questions.explanation: Thrashing occurs when active working sets exceed physical RAM, causing continuous page faults and disk I/O thrashing.
questions.hint: Continuous page faults and disk swapping.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - OS Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
questions.interviewTip: Working set model prevents thrashing by ensuring processes have sufficient page frames.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q11] What is the sequence of control flags exchanged during the standard TCP connection establishment? (Variant 1.11)
options: ACK -> SYN -> FIN
SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK
SYN -> ACK -> DATA
RST -> SYN -> ACK
questions.correctAnswer: SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK
questions.explanation: Client sends SYN with initial sequence number (ISN), Server responds with SYN-ACK, Client sends ACK to establish full-duplex session.
questions.hint: Synchronize, Synchronize-Acknowledge, Acknowledge.
questions.relatedConcept: Operations & Supply Chain - TCP 3-Way Handshake & Flow Control
questions.interviewTip: TCP 3-way handshake sequence is a universal computer network interview question.

questions.question: [Operations & Supply Chain • Test 1 • Q12] In SOLID principles, what does the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) enforce? (Variant 1.12)
options: Every class must inherit from exactly one parent.
Classes should be open for modification and closed for extension.
Dependencies must be hardcoded statically.
Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without altering program correctness.
questions.correctAnswer: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of its subclasses without altering program correctness.
questions.explanation: LSP guarantees that derived classes honor the contract and behavior expectations established by the base type.
questions.hint: Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types.

questions.question: [Startup & Entrepreneurship • Test 1 • Q1] If a startup has $1,200,000 in bank balance and net monthly burn rate of $75,000, what is its remaining runway?
options: 8 months
16 months (Runway = Total Cash / Net Monthly Burn).
12 months
24 months
questions.correctAnswer: 16 months (Runway = Total Cash / Net Monthly Burn).
questions.explanation: Runway calculation ($1,200,000 / $75,000 = 16 months) dictates how long operations can sustain before needing additional funding or reaching cash-flow positivity.
questions.hint: Cash / Net monthly burn rate.
questions.relatedConcept: Startup & Entrepreneurship - Startup Runway & Burn Rate
questions.interviewTip: Start fundraising at least 6 months before runway expires.

questions.question: [Startup & Entrepreneurship • Test 1 • Q2] In modern Product Management, how is the RICE score calculated to prioritize roadmap initiatives?
options: (Revenue * Innovation) / Cost
Risk + Impact + Cost + Execution
(Reach + Speed) * Profit
(Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
questions.correctAnswer: (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
questions.explanation: RICE standardizes feature evaluation by factoring user reach, business impact, estimation confidence, and developer effort.
questions.hint: (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort.
questions.relatedConcept: Startup & Entrepreneurship - RICE Prioritization Framework
questions.interviewTip: Confidence score helps discount features backed by assumption rather than empirical data.

options: Physical conveyor belt breakdowns in shipping warehouses.

Seasonal weather events stopping shipping vessels.
Currency exchange rate fluctuations in global trade.

questions.explanation: Lack of visibility, order batching, and safety stock buffering at each supply chain layer create severe upstream demand distortion.
questions.hint: Small retail demand shifts cause amplified upstream swings.
questions.relatedConcept: Startup & Entrepreneurship - The Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chains
questions.interviewTip: Information sharing and Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) dampen the bullwhip effect.

title: AutoCAD - Test 1: Core Fundamentals & Patterns
description: Comprehensive technical evaluation for AutoCAD covering runtime mechanics, design principles, and problem solving.

questions.question: [AutoCAD • Test 1 • Q1] In automotive design, how does aerodynamic drag force (F_drag) scale with vehicle forward speed (v)?
options: Linear scaling: drag force doubles when speed doubles.
Quadratic scaling: drag force is proportional to the square of vehicle velocity (v^2).
Logarithmic scaling: drag plateaus above 60 mph.
Independent of speed: depends only on vehicle weight.
questions.correctAnswer: Quadratic scaling: drag force is proportional to the square of vehicle velocity (v^2).
questions.explanation: Drag equation F = 0.5 * rho * v^2 * Cd * A. Because speed is squared, doubling vehicle speed quadruples aerodynamic drag force and octuples power required.
questions.hint: Drag force scales with v^2; power scales with v^3.
questions.relatedConcept: AutoCAD - Automotive Aerodynamics & Drag Force
questions.interviewTip: Streamlined shapes (low Cd) significantly extend highway range for electric vehicles.

questions.question: [AutoCAD • Test 1 • Q2] In civil structural engineering, why is steel reinforcement embedded in the bottom zone of a simply supported concrete beam?
options: Steel reduces the self-weight of the concrete beam.
Steel prevents moisture from entering the aggregate.
Concrete expands 10x more than steel under thermal loads.
Concrete has high compressive strength but very weak tensile strength; steel handles tensile stresses developed at the bottom fibers.
questions.correctAnswer: Concrete has high compressive strength but very weak tensile strength; steel handles tensile stresses developed at the bottom fibers.
questions.explanation: A simply supported beam experiences compression on top and tension on bottom. Rebar provides ductile tensile capacity to prevent brittle failure.
questions.hint: Concrete resists compression; steel resists tension.
questions.relatedConcept: AutoCAD - Reinforced Concrete & Bar Bending Schedule
questions.interviewTip: Concrete and mild steel share nearly identical thermal expansion coefficients (~12 x 10^-6 / °C).

questions.question: [AutoCAD • Test 1 • Q3] In mechanical manufacturing drawings, what does the True Position tolerance symbol specify?
options: The maximum allowable roughness of a machined surface.
Defines a theoretical exact zone within which the center, axis, or center plane of a feature is permitted to vary from its datum.
The hardness rating of the metal alloy.
The tensile strength limit before plastic deformation.
questions.correctAnswer: Defines a theoretical exact zone within which the center, axis, or center plane of a feature is permitted to vary from its datum.
questions.explanation: True position controls location and orientation relative to datums, providing cylindrical tolerance zones that maximize manufacturing acceptance rates.
questions.hint: Exact theoretical location tolerance zone.
questions.relatedConcept: AutoCAD - Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T)
questions.interviewTip: GD&T avoids tight coordinate tolerances and facilitates interchangeable parts.

questions.question: [AutoCAD • Test 1 • Q4] How does an electric vehicle (EV/HEV) capture kinetic energy during deceleration?
options: Friction brake pads compress piezoelectric quartz crystals.
Exhaust turbines harvest hot gas pressure during braking.
The transmission shifts into high gear to accelerate the flywheel.
The electric traction motor operates as a generator, converting vehicle momentum into electrical energy that recharges the traction battery pack.
questions.correctAnswer: The electric traction motor operates as a generator, converting vehicle momentum into electrical energy that recharges the traction battery pack.
questions.explanation: Regenerative braking switches the inverter firing sequence so counter-electromotive force slows wheels while rectifying current into the high-voltage pack.
questions.hint: Electric motor functions as a generator during braking.
questions.relatedConcept: AutoCAD - HEV Powertrain & Regenerative Braking
questions.interviewTip: Regenerative braking reduces mechanical brake pad wear by over 70%.

questions.question: [Project Management (Civil) • Test 1 • Q1] In automotive design, how does aerodynamic drag force (F_drag) scale with vehicle forward speed (v)?
options: Linear scaling: drag force doubles when speed doubles.
Logarithmic scaling: drag plateaus above 60 mph.
Independent of speed: depends only on vehicle weight.
Quadratic scaling: drag force is proportional to the square of vehicle velocity (v^2).
questions.correctAnswer: Quadratic scaling: drag force is proportional to the square of vehicle velocity (v^2).
questions.explanation: Drag equation F = 0.5 * rho * v^2 * Cd * A. Because speed is squared, doubling vehicle speed quadruples aerodynamic drag force and octuples power required.
questions.hint: Drag force scales with v^2; power scales with v^3.
questions.relatedConcept: Project Management (Civil) - Automotive Aerodynamics & Drag Force
questions.interviewTip: Streamlined shapes (low Cd) significantly extend highway range for electric vehicles.

questions.question: [Project Management (Civil) • Test 1 • Q2] In civil structural engineering, why is steel reinforcement embedded in the bottom zone of a simply supported concrete beam?
options: Steel reduces the self-weight of the concrete beam.
Concrete has high compressive strength but very weak tensile strength; steel handles tensile stresses developed at the bottom fibers.
Steel prevents moisture from entering the aggregate.
Concrete expands 10x more than steel under thermal loads.
questions.correctAnswer: Concrete has high compressive strength but very weak tensile strength; steel handles tensile stresses developed at the bottom fibers.
questions.explanation: A simply supported beam experiences compression on top and tension on bottom. Rebar provides ductile tensile capacity to prevent brittle failure.
questions.hint: Concrete resists compression; steel resists tension.
questions.relatedConcept: Project Management (Civil) - Reinforced Concrete & Bar Bending Schedule
questions.interviewTip: Concrete and mild steel share nearly identical thermal expansion coefficients (~12 x 10^-6 / °C).

questions.question: [Project Management (Civil) • Test 1 • Q3] In mechanical manufacturing drawings, what does the True Position tolerance symbol specify?
options: The maximum allowable roughness of a machined surface.
The hardness rating of the metal alloy.
The tensile strength limit before plastic deformation.
Defines a theoretical exact zone within which the center, axis, or center plane of a feature is permitted to vary from its datum.
questions.correctAnswer: Defines a theoretical exact zone within which the center, axis, or center plane of a feature is permitted to vary from its datum.
questions.explanation: True position controls location and orientation relative to datums, providing cylindrical tolerance zones that maximize manufacturing acceptance rates.
questions.hint: Exact theoretical location tolerance zone.
questions.relatedConcept: Project Management (Civil) - Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T)
questions.interviewTip: GD&T avoids tight coordinate tolerances and facilitates interchangeable parts.

questions.question: [Project Management (Civil) • Test 1 • Q4] How does an electric vehicle (EV/HEV) capture kinetic energy during deceleration?
options: Friction brake pads compress piezoelectric quartz crystals.
The electric traction motor operates as a generator, converting vehicle momentum into electrical energy that recharges the traction battery pack.
Exhaust turbines harvest hot gas pressure during braking.
The transmission shifts into high gear to accelerate the flywheel.
questions.correctAnswer: The electric traction motor operates as a generator, converting vehicle momentum into electrical energy that recharges the traction battery pack.
questions.explanation: Regenerative braking switches the inverter firing sequence so counter-electromotive force slows wheels while rectifying current into the high-voltage pack.
questions.hint: Electric motor functions as a generator during braking.
questions.relatedConcept: Project Management (Civil) - HEV Powertrain & Regenerative Braking
questions.interviewTip: Regenerative braking reduces mechanical brake pad wear by over 70%.

title: Psychology (Health Science) - Test 1: Core Fundamentals & Patterns

questions.question: [Psychology (Health Science) • Test 1 • Q1] In nanomedicine and oncology, what is the Enhanced Permeability and Retention (EPR) effect?
options: Nanoparticles dissolve exclusively in stomach hydrochloric acid.
Magnetic fields pull nanoparticles across healthy cell membranes.
Nanoparticles enter cells by destroying lipid bilayers irreversibly.
Nanoparticles preferentially accumulate in tumor tissues due to leaky, hyperpermeable tumor vasculature and defective lymphatic drainage.
questions.correctAnswer: Nanoparticles preferentially accumulate in tumor tissues due to leaky, hyperpermeable tumor vasculature and defective lymphatic drainage.
questions.explanation: Rapid tumor angiogenesis creates fenestrated blood vessels allowing 20-200 nm nanocarriers to extravasate into tumor parenchyma passively.
questions.hint: Leaky tumor blood vessels + poor lymphatic drainage = passive accumulation.
questions.relatedConcept: Psychology (Health Science) - Nanoparticle Targeted Drug Delivery (EPR Effect)
questions.interviewTip: Pegylation of nanoparticles extends blood circulation half-life by evading reticuloendothelial clearance.

questions.question: [Psychology (Health Science) • Test 1 • Q2] In psychological assessment and CBT, what characterizes the cognitive distortion known as 'Catastrophizing'?
options: Attributing success entirely to one's own innate talent.
Anticipating the absolute worst-case scenario and viewing it as unbearable, despite objective evidence suggesting it is unlikely.
Remembering past events with selective positive nostalgia.
Refusing to accept negative emotional states as valid.
questions.correctAnswer: Anticipating the absolute worst-case scenario and viewing it as unbearable, despite objective evidence suggesting it is unlikely.
questions.explanation: Catastrophizing exaggerates potential negative outcomes, fueling anxiety and depressive spirals. Cognitive restructuring reframes these automatic thoughts.
questions.hint: Predicting worst-case scenarios without proportional evidence.
questions.relatedConcept: Psychology (Health Science) - Cognitive Distortions in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
questions.interviewTip: Decatastrophizing exercises ask: 'What is the most likely realistic outcome?'

questions.question: [Psychology (Health Science) • Test 1 • Q3] In genetic engineering, what is the prerequisite for the Cas9 endonuclease to bind and cleave target double-stranded DNA?
options: A reverse transcriptase enzyme bound to the ribosome.
Complete absence of ATP in the nucleus.
Target DNA must be fully methylated.
Presence of a short Protospacer Adjacent Motif (PAM) sequence adjacent to the target guide RNA binding site.
questions.correctAnswer: Presence of a short Protospacer Adjacent Motif (PAM) sequence adjacent to the target guide RNA binding site.
questions.explanation: Cas9 interrogates DNA by first recognizing the PAM sequence (typically 5'-NGG-3' for SpCas9) before unwinding DNA and pairing with the guide RNA.
questions.hint: PAM sequence recognition is required for Cas9 cleavage.
questions.relatedConcept: Psychology (Health Science) - CRISPR-Cas9 Mechanism & PAM Sequence
questions.interviewTip: Engineered Cas variants target alternative PAM sequences to expand genome editing versatility.

questions.question: [Psychology (Health Science) • Test 1 • Q4] What is the primary objective of Phase I human clinical drug trials?
options: Compare long-term efficacy against existing market-standard drugs in thousands of patients (Phase III).
Evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and determine maximum tolerated dose (MTD) in a small group of healthy volunteers.
Post-marketing surveillance and rare adverse event reporting (Phase IV).
Synthesize chemical compounds in laboratory test tubes.
questions.correctAnswer: Evaluate safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and determine maximum tolerated dose (MTD) in a small group of healthy volunteers.
questions.explanation: Phase I tests safety/dose (20-100 participants), Phase II evaluates preliminary efficacy and side effects, Phase III confirms therapeutic benefit at scale.
questions.hint: Phase I = Safety, dosage, and pharmacokinetics.
questions.relatedConcept: Psychology (Health Science) - Clinical Trial Phases & Objectives
questions.interviewTip: Adherence to ICH-GCP guidelines is mandatory across all clinical phases.

questions.question: [Genetic Engineering • Test 1 • Q11] In genetic engineering, what is the prerequisite for the Cas9 endonuclease to bind and cleave target double-stranded DNA? (Variant 1.11)

questions.question: [UI/UX (Design) • Test 1 • Q2] What does Fitts's Law predict about user interaction with on-screen target elements?
options: The time required to rapidly move to a target is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target.
Users can hold at most 7 items in short-term memory (Miller's Law).
Decision time increases logarithmically with number of choices (Hick's Law).
Users perceive objects close together as belonging to the same group.
questions.correctAnswer: The time required to rapidly move to a target is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target.
questions.explanation: Fitts's law dictates that primary call-to-action buttons should be larger and closer to the user's cursor/thumb reach zone.
questions.hint: Target size and distance dictate acquisition time.
questions.relatedConcept: UI/UX (Design) - Fitts's Law in Interface Usability
questions.interviewTip: Screen corners and edges have infinite theoretical width because cursor cannot overshoot them.

questions.question: [UI/UX (Design) • Test 1 • Q3] According to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA), what is the minimum contrast ratio required for standard body text?

4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text >= 18pt or bold >= 14pt).
10:1 strictly across dark mode interfaces.
questions.correctAnswer: 4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text >= 18pt or bold >= 14pt).
questions.explanation: WCAG AA compliance mandates at least 4.5:1 contrast for normal text to ensure readability for users with moderate visual impairments.

questions.relatedConcept: Graphic Design - Typographic Hierarchy & Visual Scanning
questions.interviewTip: Maintain high line-height (1.5 - 1.6) on body text to maximize reading comfort.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q14] What does Fitts's Law predict about user interaction with on-screen target elements? (Variant 1.14)
options: Users can hold at most 7 items in short-term memory (Miller's Law).
The time required to rapidly move to a target is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target.
Decision time increases logarithmically with number of choices (Hick's Law).
Users perceive objects close together as belonging to the same group.
questions.correctAnswer: The time required to rapidly move to a target is a function of the ratio between distance to the target and width of the target.
questions.explanation: Fitts's law dictates that primary call-to-action buttons should be larger and closer to the user's cursor/thumb reach zone.
questions.hint: Target size and distance dictate acquisition time.
questions.relatedConcept: Graphic Design - Fitts's Law in Interface Usability
questions.interviewTip: Screen corners and edges have infinite theoretical width because cursor cannot overshoot them.

questions.question: [Graphic Design • Test 1 • Q15] According to Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA), what is the minimum contrast ratio required for standard body text? (Variant 1.15)
options: 2.0:1 for all text elements.
7:1 for all text (this is AAA level).
10:1 strictly across dark mode interfaces.
4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text >= 18pt or bold >= 14pt).
questions.correctAnswer: 4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text >= 18pt or bold >= 14pt).
questions.explanation: WCAG AA compliance mandates at least 4.5:1 contrast for normal text to ensure readability for users with moderate visual impairments.
questions.hint: 4.5:1 for standard text; 3:1 for large text.
questions.relatedConcept: Graphic Design - WCAG Accessibility Color Contrast
questions.interviewTip: Never rely on color alone to convey error states or interactive affordances.
